title: SLO Provenance and Incident Evidence Catalog
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Summary:

This document defines the SLO provenance model used by Redwood Inference, catalogues the types of evidence that must be captured for SLO deviations and incidents, and provides operational runbooks for collection, verification, retention, and automated tagging. The intent is to make SLO changes, burn events, and incident forensics reproducible and auditable so that rollbacks, postmortems, and compliance requests can be completed with minimal friction.

Why this matters:
- SLO numbers are decisions backed by assumptions (traffic mix, tail latency, queueing behavior). If we can tie an SLO deviation back to the exact metric definitions, instrumentation version, and dataset used for synthetic canaries, we can avoid wasted investigation time.
- Regulatory and enterprise customers sometimes request evidence of service behavior and mitigation steps; a consistent evidence catalog speeds responses.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all services in model-serving and control-plane domains (service prefixes: inference-, router-, cache-, telemetry-).
- Covers: SLO definitions, error-budget burn windows, capacity decisions, canary results, synthetic canaries, trace samples, logs, and KV cache snapshots.
- Cross-team owners: eng-sre (primary), eng-serving-runtime (secondary), product (stakeholder for SLO changes).

Core concepts and definitions:
1) SLO Provenance Record (SPR) — the canonical artifact for an SLO decision. Every SLO (new or modified) must have a SPR describing: service, metric name + promql, measurement window, SLI/SLI computation version (git SHA), alerting rules, last verification canary ID, and author.
2) Evidence Item — any artifact produced during an incident or verification that explains behavior (e.g., trace.zip, canary-report.html, capacity-snapshot.csv, model-quantization-config.txt).
3) Chain of Custody — who collected an Evidence Item, when, via what automation, and where it is stored.
4) Evidence Catalog — a human- and machine-readable index that maps SPRs and incidents to Evidence Items.

Required metadata fields (minimal SPR):
- service: inference-embed-01
- slo_id: slo_inference_p99_latency_v1
- metric_promql: sum(rate(inference_requests_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)
- measurement_window: 30d
- objective: 99th percentile <= 300ms
- sli_implementation_ref: git+ssh://git.redwood/repo.git@a1b2c3d
- alert_rule_id: alert_slo_p99_latency
- last_verified_canary: canary-2025-11-02-7
- created_by: jordan.kim@redwood.ai
- created_at: 2025-03-10T11:32:00Z

Evidence Catalog structure and storage:
- Storage locations (examples):
  - Primary evidence store: s3://redwood-evidence/eng-sre/{service}/{slo_id}/{YYYY}/{artifact}
  - Hot-forensics: elastic-archive index 'evidence-hot' for 90-day searchability
  - Long-term cold archive: gs://redwood-archive/slo-provenance/{service}/{slo_id}/ (7-year retention for enterprise customers on contract)
- Indexing: Each Evidence Item must be registered in the Evidence Catalog (Elasticsearch index: evidence-catalog-2026) with fields: evidence_id, slo_id, incident_id (optional), collected_by, collection_method, checksum (sha256), storage_uri, tags, collected_at. Automation (see runbook) will register items automatically when possible.

Evidence types and acceptance criteria:
- Synthetic Canary Report (HTML/JSON): must include canary config (model version, input distribution), pass/fail thresholds, histogram of latencies, and links to underlying traces. Acceptance: pass_rate >= 99% on control cohort, artifacts stored with canary id.
- Trace Sample (zip of spans / jaeger-export): must contain sampling seed, and include spans for request lifecycle from ingress -> model-host -> kv-cache. Acceptance: at least 3 full request traces for each affected tenant in a burn window.
- Metrics Snapshot (Prometheus exposition): a 5-minute scrape of all SLO-related metrics, saved as metrics-snapshot-{timestamp}.prom. Acceptance: must include raw counters and histogram buckets; saved with prom-version tag.
- Capacity Snapshot (CSV): node counts, GPU model, kernel version, queue depths, scheduling latency percentiles. Acceptance: snapshot within 5 minutes of incident start, stored and linked.
- Configuration Deltas (git diff / config snapshot): differences in rollout config, autoscale policies, routing policies, model-variant pins. Acceptance: must reference the git SHA and be saved as text.
- Human Notes (post-incident timeline): one structured timeline entry per action with timestamp, actor, and outcome. Acceptance: no free-form prose; must use the provided timeline template below.

Operational runbook: collecting evidence during an SLO burn or incident
1) When SLO deviation alert fires (owner: oncall):
   a) Record the alert id and timestamp in the Incident Ticket (JIRA/INC) immediately.
   b) Trigger the evidence-collector job: /opt/ops/bin/collect-evidence --incident $INC --service $SERVICE --window 15m
   c) The collector will gather: 5-minute metrics snapshot, 10 trace samples (if sampling rate allows), current config, and a capacity snapshot. It uploads to the primary evidence store and registers entries to the evidence catalog.
2) If oncall suspects model-level regression:
   a) Capture model ABI: /opt/ops/bin/model-info --host inference-node-12 --model $MODEL > model-abi.txt
   b) Tag evidence with model:{model}@{sha} and add 'model-regression' tag.
3) If degraded latency but normal error rate:
   a) Collect end-to-end traces with debug sampling for 10 minutes.
   b) Collect KV cache hit-rate histogram and eviction metrics.
4) After initial triage (within 60 minutes):
   a) Owner uploads structured timeline using template (see below).
   b) Evidence items must be attached to incident ticket and referenced in postmortem draft.

Structured timeline template (copy into incident ticket):
- 2026-02-11T14:03:12Z | Alert fired | alert_slo_p99_latency | oncall@redwood.ai | initial_snooze=10m
- 2026-02-11T14:05:41Z | Evidence collector started | collector-run-57 | s3://redwood-evidence/... | artifacts=5
- 2026-02-11T14:18:07Z | Canary failing | canary-2026-02-11-3 | failure_mode=tail-latency
- 2026-02-11T15:01:00Z | Mitigation applied | toggle-route=graceful-fallback | actor=miguel.torres

Automations and integrations:
- Evidence collector (service: evidence-collector): cron and incident-triggered job that runs the standard collection recipe. Owner: eng-sre/tooling.
- Catalog registrar (service: evidence-indexer): listens for S3 put events, computes checksum, and registers ES document. Owner: eng-sre/operational-tooling.
- Canary orchestration: canary runs are tagged with canary-id and result stored in s3://canaries/{id}. The SPR must reference the last green canary id.

Retention and access policy:
- Default evidence retention: 365 days in hot store, 5 years in cold archive for enterprise contracts.
- Access: only eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime, and assigned customer-facing support for the incident may access evidence by default. Requests outside these teams must use the evidence-access request flow (see related_pages).

Verification checklist before closing incident or downgrading SLO:
- [ ] SPR verified: promql matches instrumented metric and sli_implementation_ref corresponds to deployed agent version.
- [ ] Evidence items: metrics snapshot, traces, config diffs, and capacity snapshot present and registered.
- [ ] Chain of custody entries exist for each critical artifact.
- [ ] Root cause hypothesis documented and mapped to evidence items.
- [ ] Action items and owners assigned with ETA.

Post-incident governance for SLO changes:
- Any SLO change (tighten/loosen) requires:
  1) Updated SPR and a verification canary (must be green on control cohort for 2 successive runs).
  2) A cost/latency trade-off note filed as part of PR.
  3) 3-day observational window: automated anomaly monitors run against the new objective.
- For emergency degradations (e.g., temporary SLO relaxation to preserve availability), record decision in SPR.emergency_degraded=true and link to incident_id; an explicit rollback plan must be created and executed within 72 hours.

Templates and example artifacts (copyable snippets):
- SPR example (YAML):
  ---
  service: inference-embed-01
  slo_id: slo_inference_p99_latency_v1
  objective: 0.99@300ms
  measurement_window: 30d
  sli_implementation_ref: git+ssh://git.redwood/repo.git@a1b2c3d
  last_verified_canary: canary-2025-11-02-7
  created_by: jordan.kim@redwood.ai
  created_at: 2025-03-10T11:32:00Z

- Evidence registration CLI (example):
  curl -X POST https://evidence-api.internal/register 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVIDENCE_API_TOKEN' 
    -F 'incident_id=$INC' 
    -F 'slo_id=$SLO_ID' 
    -F 'file=@metrics-snapshot.prom' 
    -F 'collected_by=collector-run-57'

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary evidence owner: eng-sre/tooling (oncall: @eng-sre/tooling).
- SPR authorship: SREs who propose SLOs create SPRs; product must be cc'd for any objective changes for customer-impacting services.
- Escalation: If evidence collection fails or cannot capture required items (e.g., trace sampling disabled), escalate to eng-sre pager and create a compliance exception ticket.

Audit and continuous improvement:
- Quarterly audit: random sample of 10 SPRs validated for presence of evidence and matching instrumentation. Owner: eng-sre/reliability-initiatives.
- Bi-annual tabletop: simulate evidence loss and validate restore/shortfall procedures.

Appendix: quick reference commands
- Start collector: /opt/ops/bin/collect-evidence --incident INC-12345 --service inference-embed-01 --window 15m
- Register artifact manually: /opt/ops/bin/register-evidence --file metrics-snapshot.prom --slo slo_inference_p99_latency_v1 --collected_by "manual"
- Query catalog (example ES): curl -s "http://es.internal/evidence-catalog-*/_search?q=slo_id:slo_inference_p99_latency_v1&size=100" | jq

Related reading:
- SLO observability pipeline spec: /confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/slo-observability-pipeline-design-and-validation-2025
- Post-incident evidence handoff: /confluence/eng-sre/incident-review/post-incident-evidence-handoff-procedure-2026
